walkthroughs.body_html: Elizabeth balanced Protestant doctrine with Catholic aesthetics. The 1559 Act of Supremacy made her Supreme Governor (not Head) of the Church; the Act of Uniformity imposed the Book of Common Prayer. The 1563 Thirty-Nine Articles defined doctrine. Initial enforcement was lenient, but the 1570 papal bull Regnans in Excelsis excommunicated Elizabeth, prompting harsher recusancy laws.

walkthroughs.h2: Why did Philip II launch the Armada?
walkthroughs.body_html: English support for Dutch rebels, Drake's 1585-86 Caribbean raids, and Mary Queen of Scots' execution in February 1587 convinced Philip II that conquest was necessary. Pope Sixtus V endorsed a crusade. The plan: 130 ships under Medina Sidonia would rendezvous with Parma's army in Flanders. Drake's 1587 Cadiz raid delayed but did not prevent sailing.

The Armada entered the Channel on 29 July 1588 (Julian). Running battles culminated at Gravelines on 8 August where English fireships broke the crescent. Driven north, the fleet circumnavigated Scotland and Ireland, losing perhaps 50 ships to storms. Victory bolstered Protestant identity and Elizabeth's Tilbury speech became iconic, though war continued until 1604.

mcqs.q: Why was the Spanish Armada defeated in 1588?
options: Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
Drake defeated the Armada single-handedly in a great sea battle.
A combination of English tactics and fireships, poor Spanish planning, and the 'Protestant wind' storms that wrecked the fleet on the return.

mcqs.q: What was the Elizabethan Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Elizabeth made England fully Protestant and banned Catholic worship outright.
A deliberate via media — a Protestant doctrine and English-language prayer book combined with some Catholic-style ceremony — designed to maximise conformity.

mcqs.q: Why did Henry VIII break with Rome?
options: Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
Primarily for an annulment from Catherine of Aragon, but also to seize Church wealth and assert royal supremacy — not for Protestant theological reasons.
Because he wanted England to become Protestant.
